identity.title: The “Cosmic Seagull”: A Highly Magnified Disk-like Galaxy at z ≃ 2.8 behind the Bullet Cluster

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate, image and make moment maps

method.value: Pipeline scripts, concat, uvcontsub, clean (Briggs), immoments

evidence.quote: Moment maps were produced using task immoments, excluding pixels below 4$\sigma$.

key_parameters.value: robust = 0.5; moment maps exclude pixels below 4 sigma

evidence.quote: Moment maps were produced using task immoments, excluding pixels below 4$\sigma$.

method.value: LENSTOOL Bayesian optimisation of a nearby galaxy PIEMD, constrained by CO centroids, starting from published cluster model

evidence.quote: We fixed the galaxy position (X,Y), adopt a Pseudo-Isothermal Elliptical Mass Distribution (cite: 2005MNRAS.356..309L), and optimize the remaining parameters with broad uniform priors.

fitting.value: Bayesian optimisation with broad uniform priors

evidence.quote: optimize the remaining parameters with broad uniform priors

validation.value: rmsi = 0.09" and chi2/dof of 1.2; magnification uncertainty from +-1 sigma models gives 10%

evidence.quote: a $\chi^2$ per degree of freedom of $1.2$

method.value: Ray-trace A1 and A2 through best-fit lens model

evidence.quote: we ‘unlensed’ the observed images, $\mathscr{A}1$ and $\mathscr{A}2$ (Figure [2](#source_rec)), to the source plane

analysis_steps.goal: Fit rotation curve and derive dynamical mass

method.value: 2D arctan velocity model fit with four free parameters, centered on the continuum peak; thick-disk approximation

evidence.quote: we fit the two-dimensional velocity map by assuming an arctan velocity profile model

key_parameters.value: free parameters: V_asym, r_t, PA, inclination

evidence.quote: the asymptotic rotational velocity $V_{\rm asym}$, the turnover radius $\rm r_t$ (cite: 1997AJ....114.2402C), the position angle $PA$, and the disk inclination $i$

assumptions.value: thick disk; dynamical center at the continuum peak

evidence.quote: we consider a thick disk approximation

validation.value: Freeman exponential disk model tried but gave no improved fit

evidence.quote: A Freeman model (exponential disk) was also tried, but this did not provide an improved fit.

validation.value: consistent with Gonzalez et al. 2010 stellar mass

evidence.quote: consistent with previous results within the errors (cite: 2010ApJ...720..245G)

findings_qualitative.value: Rotation curve keeps rising to 2.5 kpc (~1.6 r_1/2,CO), with no evidence of a decline

evidence.quote: the rotational velocity increases as a function of galactocentric radius as far as our observations extend

findings_qualitative.value: A third unpredicted lensed image (A0) was found

evidence.quote: This image was not predicted by any previous lensing model

claims.hypothesis: Does the high-z galaxy rotation curve decline at large radius?
claims.experiment: Fit arctan model to the source-plane CO(3-2) velocity map
claims.result: Rotation curve rising out to 2.5 kpc
claims.finding: No evidence of a decreasing rotation curve

evidence.quote: We find no evidence for a decreasing rotation curve

claims.hypothesis: Is the galaxy gas dominated and not a major merger?
claims.experiment: Dynamical, SED stellar and CO gas masses; continuum-kinematic centre coincidence
claims.finding: Gas-dominated disk, not in a major merger

evidence.quote: this galaxy is not involved in a major merging event

why_this_method.value: A0 used for stellar mass because it is little affected by neighbors and differential magnification

evidence.quote: this image is preferred as it is not significantly affected by near neighbors

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Freeman exponential disk model gave no improved fit

evidence.quote: A Freeman model (exponential disk) was also tried, but this did not provide an improved fit.

reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Lens model and kinematic code are not available, so the numeric results cannot be redone from the text alone.
